event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: EQT’s 2024 Form 10-K rarely mentions the COVID-19 pandemic by name, yet several passages describe conditions that are strongly associated with the pandemic era—namely supply-chain disruptions, shortages of labor and equipment, and knock-on effects such as delayed well completions and higher operating costs. These references frame the threat both retrospectively (actual production and cost impacts in 2022-2023) and prospectively (the possibility that new disruptions could force changes to the 2024 drilling schedule). Because the filing date is almost four years after the WHO declaration of the pandemic, the Time Decay Principle moves the risk out of the “recent” category and into the 4-to-10-year “medium-term” window; accordingly, the highest permissible snippet scores are in the mid-single digits. The evidence is largely qualitative and lacks quantified dollar impacts, but one sentence does acknowledge measurable operational headwinds in early 2023. Overall, the company conveys a moderate, still-pertinent risk: COVID-19-related supply-chain and labor constraints have already affected results and could do so again, yet the language is generic and the immediacy of the crisis has ebbed, tempering the severity scores.

evidence_list.snippet: • supply chain disruptions or labor shortage impacts;

components.reason: Explicitly cites ‘supply chain disruptions,’ an accepted pandemic-linked risk factor.
Also references ‘labor shortage impacts,’ another common pandemic consequence.
Bullet-point wording is generic and gives no magnitude or timing.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly lists two pandemic-related hazards but in a generic, boiler-plate manner, warranting a moderate score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: • shortages of or delays in obtaining equipment, rigs, materials, qualified personnel or water (for hydraulic fracturing activities);

components.reason: Highlights shortages and delays in critical inputs—classic supply-chain stressors.
Lacks event attribution or quantified impact, reducing specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures both material and labor shortages but remains forward-looking and unquantified, producing a score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Our sales volume and operating expenses on a per Mcfe basis during the first half of 2023 were negatively impacted by fewer wells turned-in-line during 2022 compared to our 2022 planned development schedule due to third-party supply chain constraints.

components.reason: States an actual, realized negative impact on sales volume and costs.
Specifies the recent timeframe (first half of 2023), demonstrating recency.
Links impact to ‘third-party supply chain constraints,’ aligning with pandemic-era disruptions.
No dollar magnitude provided, limiting precision.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete, recent operational harm tied to supply-chain problems, but without financial quantification; capped at 6 to respect medium-term timing.

evidence_list.snippet: Future supply chain constraints or declines in natural gas prices may result in adjustments to our 2024 planned development schedule or the development schedule of non-operated wells in which we have a working interest.

components.reason: Flags potential future disruptions to the 2024 schedule caused by supply-chain issues.
Conveys operational repercussions (schedule adjustments) if the risk materialises.
Forward-looking, generic wording and no mention of COVID-19 or quantified impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies prospective supply-chain risk for 2024 but remains speculative and generic, meriting a score of 3.
